findings.highlight: My consciousness is breaking apart.
findings.evidenceJa: 意識が断線する。
findings.governingReading: Shirou’s consciousness disconnects like a severed wire.
findings.explanation: The English replaces loss of connection with general fragmentation, weakening the route’s recurring circuitry model.

findings.highlight: an impossibly vast expanse
findings.evidenceJa: 永遠に到達できない長さ
findings.governingReading: A mere hundred meters has become a length he can never reach across for eternity.
findings.explanation: The English conveys impossible scale but removes endless duration and the inability to arrive.

findings.highlight: The ceiling’s crumbling down, and the ground is becoming a pile of rubble.
findings.evidenceJa: 天蓋はところどころが崩れ、荒野のようだった地上は、瓦礫の山
findings.governingReading: Parts of the canopy collapse while the formerly wasteland-like ground becomes a mountain of rubble.
findings.explanation: The English removes partial distribution, the prior wasteland comparison, and the growing mountain scale.

findings.highlight: An inescapable death by skewering.
findings.evidenceJa: 逃げ様のない串刺し刑
findings.governingReading: The hundreds of internal blades constitute an inescapable punishment or execution by impalement.
findings.explanation: The English keeps lethal skewering but removes the punitive execution image.

findings.highlight: I am the bone of my sword.
findings.evidenceJa: 体は剣で出来ている。
findings.governingReading: The narration states directly that Shirou’s body is made of swords.
findings.explanation: The English substitutes a familiar incantation line, changing body composition into the metaphorical “bone” formula.

findings.highlight: I’m crumbling apart. I’ll shatter if I continue.
findings.evidenceJa: 割れる。これ以上は割れる。
findings.governingReading: Shirou is cracking and will split if he goes any farther.
findings.explanation: “Crumbling” prematurely supplies gradual disintegration and weakens the repeated crack/split wording.

findings.highlight: I’ll still make it.
findings.evidenceJa: まだ間に合う。
findings.governingReading: Shirou judges that there is still time to stop and preserve himself.
findings.explanation: The English promotes remaining opportunity into a confident prediction that he personally will succeed.

findings.highlight: My body’s dying
findings.evidenceJa: この体は手遅れ
findings.governingReading: His body is already beyond saving.
findings.explanation: “Dying” removes the explicit point of no return.

findings.highlight: I won’t lose myself for about a day
findings.evidenceJa: 一日ぐらいは意味を失わずに済む
findings.governingReading: Stopping now may let Shirou avoid losing meaning for roughly a day.
findings.explanation: The English resolves abstract existential meaning into the self as a stable object.

findings.highlight: The part that administers the principle of behavior, the linkage to pleasure.
findings.evidenceJa: 行動原理、即ち快楽の連動を司るところ
findings.governingReading: The nucleus accumbens is described as governing the link between behavioral principle and pleasure.
findings.explanation: The English fragment makes the anatomy administer a “principle” and leaves the linkage apposition malformed.

findings.highlight: without it, humans would become beasts
findings.evidenceJa: それがない人間は獣と同じ
findings.governingReading: Humans without pursuit of pleasure are said to be the same as beasts.
findings.explanation: The English changes a comparison of present condition into a hypothetical transformation.

findings.highlight: I want to keep my memory for as long as I can.
findings.evidenceJa: 自分が自分のままでいる事に、身を食むほどに執着している
findings.governingReading: Shirou clings with self-devouring intensity to remaining himself.
findings.explanation: The English narrows existential self-continuity to retaining memory and removes the consuming force of attachment.

findings.highlight: doesn’t stop the memories from fading
findings.evidenceJa: 記憶の消失を止められない
findings.governingReading: Even mutilated pain cannot stop memory from disappearing.
findings.explanation: “Fading” weakens categorical disappearance into gradual dimming.

findings.highlight: I probably won’t remember what I need to do.
findings.evidenceJa: 自分が誰か、何をするかを、きっと無くしてしまっている
findings.governingReading: Even if he arrives, Shirou will surely have lost both who he is and what he is to do.
findings.explanation: The English drops identity entirely and weakens certainty to probability and loss to failed recollection.

findings.highlight: Somewhere outside my body, there’s a big reason.
findings.evidenceJa: 大きな理由が、体の外にあって
findings.governingReading: A great reason exists outside Shirou’s failing body.
findings.explanation: “Somewhere” makes the relation spatially vague and “big” weakens existential importance.

findings.highlight: So I have to fulfill my role.
findings.evidenceJa: おまえは、おまえの役目を、果たさないと。
findings.governingReading: A surviving voice addresses Shirou as “you” twice and commands him to fulfill his role.
findings.explanation: The English changes the dissociated second-person self-command into ordinary first-person resolve.

findings.highlight: I couldn’t breathe if I had all day to do it.
findings.evidenceJa: たった一息の空気が、一日かけても吸えずにいる
findings.governingReading: Even given an entire day, Shirou remains unable to draw a single breath of air.
findings.explanation: The English turns an experienced time-dilated failure into a hypothetical inability.

findings.highlight: I manage to keep myself.
findings.evidenceJa: 踏み止まった。
findings.governingReading: During the fall, Shirou arrests his descent or holds his footing.
findings.explanation: The English replaces concrete physical resistance with vague self-preservation.

findings.highlight: All the shards of my existence are gathered onto a tiny foothold.
findings.evidenceJa: 爪の先ほどの足場に、全存在を留まらせる
findings.governingReading: Shirou holds his entire existence on a foothold no larger than a fingernail tip.
findings.explanation: The English invents shards of existence and removes the exact fingernail scale and act of holding fast.

findings.highlight: The foothold breaks.
findings.evidenceJa: 足場は、崩れて
findings.governingReading: The sentence itself breaks off as the foothold begins to collapse.
findings.explanation: The English completes both syntax and event, removing the enacted interruption.

findings.highlight: There’s no meaning of behavior.
findings.evidenceJa: 行動理由が喪い。
findings.governingReading: The reason for action is lost in the sequence from principle to purpose.
findings.explanation: “Meaning of behavior” is unnatural and collapses reason into the adjacent existential meaning.

findings.highlight: The meaning behind my existence disappears.
findings.evidenceJa: 何の為に誰の為に存在しているのか消失した
findings.governingReading: Shirou loses for what and for whom he exists.
findings.explanation: The English generalizes existential meaning and removes both purpose and beneficiary.

findings.highlight: My arms won’t move
findings.evidenceJa: その腕が動く事はない。
findings.governingReading: That arm will move under no possible reason.
findings.explanation: The English pluralizes the arm and turns a distanced reference into ordinary possession.

findings.highlight: language, neopallium, and cerebrum are lost
findings.evidenceJa: 言語野はおろか新皮質全般、他三部を含む大脳まで消失
findings.governingReading: Not only language areas but the entire neocortex and even the cerebrum including three other divisions are gone.
findings.explanation: The English reduces language anatomy to “language,” uses the imprecise “neopallium,” and removes the exhaustive regional scope.

findings.highlight: Spinning the eight verses.
findings.evidenceJa: 八節を紡ぐ。
findings.governingReading: The remaining mechanism weaves the eight sections of the incantation.
findings.explanation: “Verses” imposes a poetic unit and the English remains a sentence fragment without an agent.

findings.highlight: It’s programmed to swing the sword
findings.evidenceJa: 作り上げた剣を振り上げる機能
findings.governingReading: The machine-like remnant has the function to raise the sword it made.
findings.explanation: The English invents programming and changes raising the created sword into swinging an unspecified one.

findings.highlight: it’s a corpse
findings.evidenceJa: 残骸と変わらない
findings.governingReading: Without will to move the function, the standing form is no different from wreckage or a remnant.
findings.explanation: The English changes mechanical remains into a biological corpse, weakening the machine comparison.

findings.highlight: even without human intelligence
findings.evidenceJa: 人工の知能がなくとも
findings.governingReading: Even without artificial intelligence, machines in this world weave dreams.
findings.explanation: The English directly replaces artificial intelligence with human intelligence, reversing the machine-specific premise.

findings.highlight: A recitation of words without meaning.
findings.evidenceJa: 意味さえ解らない文字の羅列
findings.governingReading: The promise has become a sequence of written characters whose meanings are no longer understood.
findings.explanation: The English turns unreadable symbols into spoken words being recited.

findings.highlight: A small hope that I remembered until the very end.
findings.evidenceJa: 果たされるべき、小さな希望
findings.governingReading: The small hope remembered to the end is something that must be fulfilled.
findings.explanation: The English preserves final memory but removes the obligation that drives the dead mechanism onward.
